title: The Mainframe — Local-First Life Management
description: A private, offline-first life management app for courses, projects, goals, ideas, purchases, and ventures. Built with Tauri, React, Rust, and SQLite.

sections.heading: Built for people whose work does not fit in one list
sections.text: Built for people whose work does not fit in one list Most life tools are either a generic task list you have to reshape around your life, or a workspace so broad that maintaining it becomes the work. The Mainframe starts from the lists a person actually keeps: studies, builds, acquisitions, long-term goals, and ventures. Developers and solo builders Several builds, courses, and side projects running in parallel with no single place that shows all of them. Students and career switchers Certification tracks, study material, and application deadlines spread across notes, browsers, and messages. F

sections.heading: Watch it become rows
sections.text: 02 Watch it become rows Each non-empty line becomes one item, with the original line kept alongside it as raw import text. That is the whole transform: the app does not guess which domain a line belongs to, and it does not invent a due date for you. Rows in a domain list Screenshot coming with the first release.

sections.heading: See what needs attention
sections.text: 03 See what needs attention The dashboard pulls a short cross-domain shortlist and says why each entry surfaced, using plain reasons such as being overdue, being due this week, or not having been touched in a while. Cross-domain attention view Screenshot coming with the first release.

sections.heading: Stay offline, sync only when you choose
sections.text: 04 Stay offline, sync only when you choose The app reads and writes a local SQLite database on each device. When you want the same snapshot on a second device, pair once on a trusted local network and transfer a validated snapshot. LAN sync pairing Screenshot coming with the first release.

sections.heading: Four things it does, and nothing else
sections.text: Four things it does, and nothing else Each pillar is a commitment about behavior, not a feature count. Technical detail belongs further down the page. Bring in a list Paste messy plain text and start with structure. No template to fill in, no import wizard, and the source line stays attached to the row it produced. See what matters now One combined view across every domain so parallel tracks stop competing for attention in your head. Each suggestion explains why it appeared. sections.heading: What it will not do, and what you should know
sections.text: What it will not do, and what you should know Two different lists. The first is what the app will never do to you. The second is what is genuinely limited today — stated plainly, because you should know it before you put real work in. What it will not do No required account or cloud service The core workflow never calls a hosted backend. There is no sign-up, no subscription, and no telemetry service in the loop. sections.heading: Read the code before you trust it
sections.text: Read the code before you trust it The source is public, and the claims above are checkable in it. Issues and focused pull requests are welcome — the limitations are as open to discussion as the features. Include the platform, the app version or commit, reproduction steps, and relevant logs. Keep reports specific — a narrow bug with clear steps is more useful than a broad feature wish. Do not attach database files or other private data to an issue. Sanitize screenshots first.
